out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided at the hand sink behind the line.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw eggs were stored overcooked chicken in the two-door refrigerator. Raw eggs were also stored over other cooked foods and produce in one of the prep refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Discontinue storing raw foods over cooked foods. The PIC moved raw eggs to the bottom shelf during the inspection.CDI.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: foods cooked on site and held more than 24 hours are not being date marked, including cooked chicken and sliced cold cuts.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The manager, date marked the foods listed above during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers were observed reused for the storage of foods. Manufacturer containers used previously used for sour cream, burrata, grated Parmesan, and other foods were being reused, which is not permitted.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. Discontinue reusing manufacturers containers and use commercial food-grade equipment instead. The PIC discarded all the reused containers during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: several plastic home-standard colanders were being used. They were cracked, burned and deteriorated and not approved for use.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. The PIC discarded the damaged equipment to correct. CDI.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: There is no test kit located in the facility for monitoring the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solutions. The PIC could not locate a test kit for quaternary ammonia.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a quaternary ammonia test kit as soon as possible or within 10 days. The PIC ordered a test kit during the inspection.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The Person in charge could not provide employee health policy documents.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS provided the PIC with the health department model employee health policy. The PIC trained her employees during the inspection and had them complete the forms.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. The person in charge could not provide a vomit and diarrhea clean up policy.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the person in charge with the model health department policy, which she adopted.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. The food employee came in came from the back room did not wash hands before putting on gloves and preparing food. The employee said she washed her hands in the back room, but there was no hand soap, hand sink in the back room, and the hand sink was blocked.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The DHS discussed this with the person in charge during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee stated she cleaned her hands in a food preparation sink. There is a sign to the food prep sink, but there is no handsoap who provided, and it was blocked by boxes on top of it.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. The EHS discussed this requirement with the person in charge. The food employee washed their hands after this discussion. CDI.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap at the handwashing sink next to the sink. Also, the hand sink was not accessible due to boxes stored on top of it. It appeared that the hand soap was not being used.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The EHS discussed this with the person in charge. CDI.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shelled eggs were stored over ready to eat foods in one of the prep units.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The EHS discussed this with the person in charge who moved the eggs to the lower shelf. CDI.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Label on one of the spray bottles had faded away. All spray bottles must be labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The person in charge corrected this by relabeling the bottle during the inspection. CDI.
